cf.title: WAL record CRC calculated incorrectly because of underlying buffer modification

input.subject: WAL record CRC calculated incorrectly because of underlying buffer modification

verdict_reasoning: This is a real bug with buildfarm failures and a reproducer, so levels 1a and 1b pass. The visible material holds no fix: the only attachment is a debugging assertion, and message #10 rules out the one candidate. The surviving objections, replication-ondisk-2 and maintenance-fit-1, are fixable design points about the back-branch plan and an unenforced REGBUF_NO_CHANGE rule. The second CommitFest thread and any newer patch are not shown.

brief.title: Hash index modifies a WAL-registered buffer, so the record CRC is wrong
brief.problem: Buildfarm members dodo and chipmunk logged "incorrect resource manager data checksum" errors. XLogRecordAssemble() computes the record CRC over a buffer that another backend changes before the record is copied to WAL. The visible case is hashbucketcleanup() during vacuum, with wal_consistency_checking enabled.
brief.proposed_design: The attached patch is a debugging aid. It copies the registered block and asserts it is unchanged after the CRC step, so it shows the bug and does not fix it. A candidate fix in the thread skips the full-page image for REGBUF_NO_CHANGE buffers even under XLR_CHECK_CONSISTENCY, but Jeff Davis later called it not acceptable.
author_claims: The reporter reproduces the assertion failure on iterations 7, 10 and 17 of 100 runs of the hash_index test with wal_consistency_checking = all.
A reduced psql reproducer with concurrent insert, drop and vacuum hits the same assertion.
The reporter reproduced the issue on a 2018 commit, so it is not a recent regression.
The thread says the candidate REGBUF_NO_CHANGE change stops the reduced reproducer from failing.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund, Thomas Munro, Jeff Davis, Michael Paquier and Robert Haas replied in May 2024. No fix is agreed: Jeff wants hash indexes to follow the locking rules or copy the page as XLogSaveBufferForHint() does, and nobody has answered why hash indexes avoid the exclusive lock.
unclear: The CommitFest entry dates from 2026-10 and lists Greg Burd and a second thread, but that thread and any newer patch are not shown.
No visible patch fixes the bug; the only attachment is the assertion patch.
The thread does not say how to fix back branches, which lack REGBUF_NO_CHANGE.
No one has measured the cost of taking an exclusive lock on the bucket page in hashbucketcleanup().
Jeff Davis reports that _hash_freeovflpage() registers a buffer with REGBUF_NO_CHANGE but without REGBUF_NO_IMAGE, and the thread does not settle it.

objections.title: No back-branch fix that keeps hash WAL records replayable
objections.failure_scenario: An operator applies a minor release to the primary before the standby, as the upgrade notes advise against but as rolling upgrades often do. If the fix changes which blocks a hash record registers or how it registers them, the older standby fails to replay, or replays differently, and the operator finds out when replication stops.
objections.argument: Message #6 reproduces the bug on a 2018 commit, so every supported branch needs a fix. Message #5 notes that the back branches lack REGBUF_NO_CHANGE, and message #7 offers only two untested ideas. Message #10 rules out the one candidate fix, and the fixes Jeff Davis suggests (exclusive locking, or copying the page as XLogSaveBufferForHint() does) may change hash record contents or locking during replay. The CommitFest entry adds a second thread, but the material does not show it.
objections.author_must_show: Which fix goes into the back branches, and does it leave the hash WAL record format unchanged, so that standbys on older and newer minor releases replay the same records?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 reproduces the bug on a 2018 commit, and the visible material has no fix for any branch, with message #7 offering only two untried ideas. The mixed-minor-version scenario is speculative, but the missing back-branch plan is real.

objections.title: A fix that keeps REGBUF_NO_CHANGE leaves its rules unenforced
objections.failure_scenario: A later hash or extension change registers a pinned, unlocked buffer with REGBUF_NO_CHANGE but without REGBUF_NO_IMAGE. Nothing fails at insert time. Months later a buildfarm member running wal_consistency_checking, or a user standby, logs "incorrect resource manager data checksum", and someone again has to trace it back.
objections.argument: Message #8 names an invariant (REGBUF_NO_CHANGE implies REGBUF_NO_IMAGE) that no code checks, and says _hash_freeovflpage() already breaks it. Message #10 rules out the special case in message #5. This bug survived from at least 2018 (message #6), so a silent rule is not enough protection. Messages #8 and #9 prefer removing the flag, but nobody has committed to that work.
objections.author_must_show: Will the fix remove REGBUF_NO_CHANGE, or add a check that fails loudly when a caller registers an unlocked buffer that can still produce an image?

critic.reasoning: No code checks that an unlocked registered buffer can never produce an image, and messages #8 and #9 agree the flag is a weak point. The _hash_freeovflpage() case holds an exclusive lock, so it shows the missing check, not a second bug.

refuted.title: The proposal does not show the bad CRC is limited to wal_consistency_checking
refuted.failure_scenario: After a checkpoint, a hash vacuum or overflow-page free registers a buffer that another backend changes while it is being copied as a full-page image. The record is written with a CRC that does not match its data. Crash recovery or a standby then stops replay at that record and treats it as the end of WAL, so later committed records are lost.
refuted.argument: Message #8 says _hash_freeovflpage() registers a buffer with REGBUF_NO_CHANGE but without REGBUF_NO_IMAGE. Message #3 shows that an image is taken whenever needs_backup is true, and not only under XLR_CHECK_CONSISTENCY. If that buffer can change during the copy, production clusters without wal_consistency_checking are also exposed. The thread does not settle this, and the only attached patch is a debugging assertion that detects the problem but does not fix it.
refuted.author_must_show: Can any buffer registered without REGBUF_NO_IMAGE in the hash code change during a normal full-page image, and if it can, which fix covers that path?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs an unlocked buffer registered without REGBUF_NO_IMAGE. In _hash_freeovflpage() the caller holds an exclusive content lock on wbuf, so no other backend can change it during the copy, and hashbucketcleanup() passes REGBUF_NO_IMAGE.

refuted.title: Area has no engaged owner for hash index locking
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer pushes an exclusive-lock or page-copy change to hashbucketcleanup() and back-patches it without REGBUF_NO_CHANGE in the older branches. A locking or replay regression then shows up on standbys. No one who knows why hash indexes avoid the exclusive lock is available to judge it.
refuted.argument: In message #11 the author of the hash WAL work declines to answer why the lock is avoided, and message #10 says the question was asked before and not answered. The thread has no measurement of the exclusive-lock cost. It also has no plan for back branches (message #7). The 2026 CommitFest entry lists a new thread that is not shown, so this may already be addressed.
refuted.author_must_show: Who has worked out why hashbucketcleanup() avoids the exclusive lock, what does that lock cost, and how will the fix reach branches without REGBUF_NO_CHANGE?

critic.reasoning: The scenario assumes an unnamed regression from a fix nobody has written, while five committers replied and Jeff Davis proposed directions. Ownership belongs in the committability field, and the back-branch part is a duplicate of replication-ondisk-2.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The bug is a wrong WAL record CRC, and any fix changes how hash code registers buffers for WAL.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Removing or restricting REGBUF_NO_CHANGE changes the XLogRegisterBuffer() flags that extensions can use.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #6 reproduces the bug on a 2018 commit, and the back branches lack REGBUF_NO_CHANGE.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: No code checks that an unlocked registered buffer cannot produce a full-page image.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: An exclusive lock or page copy in hashbucketcleanup() adds cost to hash index vacuum, and nobody has measured it.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which fix does the current patch implement: an exclusive lock on the bucket page, a page copy as XLogSaveBufferForHint() does, or something else?
Which fix goes into the back branches, which lack REGBUF_NO_CHANGE, and does it leave the hash WAL record format unchanged?
Will the fix remove REGBUF_NO_CHANGE, or add a check that fails loudly when a caller registers an unlocked buffer that can still produce an image?
What does the chosen fix cost in hashbucketcleanup() during vacuum of a hash index under concurrent inserts?
Why does hashbucketcleanup() avoid the exclusive lock on the bucket page, and does the fix keep whatever that choice protects?

committability.owner_note: Several committers who know WAL insertion replied in May 2024, and Jeff Davis proposed fix directions. The fix also needs someone who knows the hash index locking protocol, and message #11 leaves that question unanswered.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a locking or WAL registration change in hash index vacuum on every supported branch, including replay behaviour on standbys, for the life of those branches.
committability.author_follow_up: Greg Burd created the CommitFest entry on 2026-10-27 and attached a second thread on 2026-11-03, after which CFbot reported the patch no longer needs a rebase. That thread is not shown.

priority.reason: The bad CRC is shown only for hash indexes with wal_consistency_checking enabled, but it is a real bug that causes buildfarm failures. Review cost is a guess because no fix patch was read; the change is likely small but touches WAL insertion and hash locking on all branches.

provisional_note: The fix itself could not be judged: the only visible patch is the debugging assertion, and the second thread attached to the CommitFest entry is not shown. The back-branch approach and the lock cost are unknown.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Non-volatile WAL buffer
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaced the DRAM WAL buffers with one large buffer file on persistent memory (PMEM), sized by nvwal_size, so WAL records became durable there without writes to WAL segment files. Segment files were written only in archiving mode or when the buffer was full.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not include a withdrawal reason. In the last messages the author moves to the separate "NTT / segments" patchset, which mmaps regular WAL segment files. Tomas Vondra had measured it as fast as "NTT / buffer", with the speedup almost gone when full_page_writes=off. Earlier, the author called the hard nvwal_size limit, which blocks all WAL inserts when the buffer is full, a major weak point.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In addition, "NTT / segments"
patchset is more compatible to the current PG and more friendly to
DBAs because that patchset uses WAL segment files and does not
introduce any other new WAL-related file.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track Oldest Initialized WAL Buffer Page
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an OldestInitializedPage field to XLogCtl that tracks the start address of the oldest initialized WAL buffer page, updated under WALBufMappingLock. Its purpose is to let callers check quickly, without a lock, whether a WAL record is still in the WAL buffers, and to walk the buffers from oldest to newest.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas showed that a caller can already check whether a record is in WAL buffers by comparing xlblocks[idx] with the expected page end pointer, with an atomic read if stale results are fine. He saw no need to track OldestInitializedPage. The author did not reply, and the entry was returned with feedback after the thread stalled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But I don't see the point of tracking OldestInitializedPage. It
seems cheap enough that we could, if there's a need for it, but I don't
see the need.

precedents_retrieved.title: Why enable_hashjoin Completely disables HashJoin
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes enable_hashjoin (and likewise enable_mergejoin) penalize hash join paths with disable_cost instead of not building them at all. With all three join switches off, the planner could then still pick a hash join.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said the current behavior is intended. Hash and merge joins are not always possible, so they are hard-disabled, while nestloop is always possible and gets only disable_cost so that some plan exists. Tom Lane did not want to extend disable_cost, which he called a crude hack. The author agreed nothing needed to change and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The disable-cost stuff is a crude hack that we use when
turning off a particular plan type entirely might render us
unable to generate a valid plan.  Hash join is not in that
category.

precedents_retrieved.title: Check consistency of GUC defaults between .sample.conf and pg_settings.boot_val
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the TAP test 003_check_guc.pl, with an SQL version too, so it checks that each default in postgresql.conf.sample matches pg_settings.boot_val. GUCs whose defaults depend on the platform or are set by initdb are excluded through new GUC flags (DEFAULTS_COMPILE, DEFAULTS_INITDB) and a hardcoded list of parameters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier did not want the test to depend on a hardcoded list of GUCs, because the existing test needs no such maintenance. At closing he also objected to the new backend GUC flags and to the extra logic needed for initdb-set and platform-dependent defaults, and preferred to keep 003_check_guc.pl checking parameter names only. The thread had no activity for more than 8 months, and vignesh C closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: FWIW, I am not really a fan of making this test depend on a hardcoded list of GUCs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical insert/update/delete WAL records for custom table AMs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add new WAL records representing a logical insert, update, delete (and later truncate) that do nothing at REDO time and are only processed during logical decoding, so that custom table AMs such as a columnar extension can support logical decoding/replication without extensible WAL. Later versions added SQL functions pg_logical_emit_insert/update/delete/truncate and tests using test_decoding.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch, saying that with custom WAL resource managers (his parallel extensible rmgr work) it had become less important to him. Earlier, Amit Kapila questioned whether a common heap-tuple-based format could work for all table AMs, and the patch had stopped applying, but the visible messages show no deciding objection from a reviewer.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Withdrawn for now. With custom WAL resource managers this is less
important to me.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add MAIN_RELATION_CLEANUP and TOAST_TABLE_CLEANUP options to VACUUM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds two VACUUM options, MAIN_RELATION_CLEANUP and TOAST_TABLE_CLEANUP (first named SECONDARY_RELATION_CLEANUP), so a table owner can vacuum only the main relation or only its TOAST table. It reuses VACOPT_SKIPTOAST, adds a flag to vacuum_rel() to skip the main relation, and adds matching vacuumdb support.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers questioned whether the use case justifies new options and more complex vacuum code. A TOAST table can already be vacuumed directly by name, with GRANT USAGE ON pg_toast for unprivileged roles, or through a script or SQL function. Michael Paquier suggested exposing only VACOPT_SKIPTOAST to users, and the entry was returned with feedback after no further activity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am not sure that this use-case justifies a new option and more complications in the code paths of vacuum though.

precedents_retrieved.title: SLRU data page checksums
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add checksums to SLRU pages (clog, multixact, commit timestamps, subtrans and similar), stored in the last two bytes of each page, computed on write and verified on read when data checksums are enabled. A new GUC, ignore_slru_checksum_failure, would turn verification failures into warnings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The shown messages do not include a closing decision, but they record unresolved problems. Thomas Munro pointed out that SLRU pages have no full-page-write protection, so a torn page after power loss would fail checksum verification and could stop recovery, and whole-page checksums are incompatible with the incremental redo of SLRU pages. Earlier, Alexander Korotkov noted that pg_upgrade support for the changed usable page size was missing. Andres Freund backed a different approach, adding regular page headers to SLRU blocks, which Shawn Debnath said he was working on.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: With your patch, a torn SLRU page can cause recovery to fail.

precedents_retrieved.title: Map WAL segment files on PMEM as WAL buffers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patchset maps WAL segment files that live on persistent memory (PMEM) directly into memory with libpmem and uses them as the WAL buffers, so WAL is written in place without a separate copy and write. It adds a --with-libpmem build option and a wal_pmem_map setting, and sizes the mapped buffers to min_wal_size with pre-allocation by walwriter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took it up. Jacob Champion returned it in a batch of patchsets that did not get enough reviewer interest, and he wrote that this was not a rejection and that there was little actionable feedback. Earlier messages only asked for build fixes, CI support and rebases, and the author did each of them.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As discussed in [1], we're taking this opportunity to return some
patchsets that don't appear to be getting enough reviewer interest.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. Message #7 and message #8 link the earlier thread that added REGBUF_NO_CHANGE, and message #10 already rejected the in-thread candidate fix, so there is no prior rejection reason left to raise against any visible proposal.

No user-facing contract changes. The attached patch only adds an assertion in xloginsert.c, and the thread adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog entry, pg_dump output or psql behaviour. The one compatibility topic is back branches, which lack REGBUF_NO_CHANGE (message #7). That depends on a fix that is not yet shown, and message #10 already withdrew the candidate fix, so there is no design to object to. If a fix changes hash WAL record contents in minor releases, a committer would likely ask how a standby on an older minor release replays them.
Both objections are about the WAL safety of a fix that the material does not show yet. The attached assertion patch is a debugging aid and does not change on-disk or WAL state.

This proposal does not touch privileges, authentication, or data exposure. The attached patch only adds an assertion to xloginsert.c, and the bad CRC appears only with wal_consistency_checking, which only a superuser can set. An ordinary user can already run insert and vacuum on a hash index, and nothing in the thread gives that user new reach. Whether the _hash_freeovflpage() case raised in message #8 can corrupt WAL without wal_consistency_checking is a correctness question for another angle.
This is a real bug fix, and fixing it belongs in core. The only visible patch is a debugging assertion, so the objections apply to the fix direction and not to an idea that should be rejected.

This entry fixes a bug where hash index WAL records get a wrong CRC, and no existing feature, extension or setting prevents it. The one existing mechanism that applies, copying the page as XLogSaveBufferForHint() does, is already suggested in message #8 and message #10 as a fix, so it gives no reason to reject the entry.

This is a bug report with buildfarm failures on dodo and chipmunk and a reproducer from message #1 and #4, so demand is not in question. Corrupt WAL CRCs hurt anyone who uses hash indexes with wal_consistency_checking, and the open questions are about the fix design, which other angles cover.
